The waterfall and its surroundings form an exclave of the Karkonosze National Park. It is the second highest waterfall of the national park.


== Description ==
Szklarki Falls is located at 525 metres (1,722 ft) above sea level and is 13.3 meters high. Its waters fall in a wide cascade characteristically narrowing downwards and spiraling, where it forms a plunge pool.
In 1868, an inn was opened near the waterfall, which today functions as a mountain shelter named "Kochanówka".
To enter the national park, visitors need to pay an admission fee. There is a 1-km long trail leading to the waterfall at the end of which is a viewing platform. The trail is also accessible for disabled people.
